cr_data.provenance: Alma Morganthau Wertheim, New York, NY, gift, 1920s; Descended in family; Christie's, New York, NY, sale no. 8546, lot no. 278, 4 December 1996, no sale; Greenberg Van Doren Gallery, St. Louis, 1996; (Manny Silverman Gallery, Los Angeles, California) (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "The picture is in the country but Mrs. Wiener (formerly Mrs. Alma Morganthau Wertheim) will give me the measurements, etc. later. She said Miss O'Keeffe made sketches for this while staying with her at Cos Cob, she thinks about 1922. Owned by Mrs. Paul Weiner." Abiquiú Notebooks indicates, "Pink strip on edge. Second skunk cabbage. From O'Keeffe 1957. Betty Pilkington." Pictured in 1923 New York (Anderson) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 14. See cat. nos. 1943, 1944. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.notes: Source of title: Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks.
titles.title: Skunk Cabbage

description: A pale, greenish blue leaf extends from the bottom to the top of the composition. In front of the leaf is a curling, dark red skunk cabbage flower. The plants are set against a textured background in shades of green, yellow, and black.
imageCaption: Image courtesy of a scanned transparency made for Georgia O'Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné. This image has not been color proofed and may differ from the original. It will be replaced when newer photography becomes available.
